title: COMPLEMENTATION OF ANAEROBIC BIOREACTOR FOR WASTE DEGRADATION FROM LONG-TERM HUMAN MISSIONS - RE-ISSUE
description: Re-supply and waste management are a critical elements of a crewed space exploration. A significant part of pressurized cargo uploaded mass consists of packaging material (0.3 kg/person/day) which cannot be recycled into resources and become mission waste. Currently, no waste management practice has been implemented in space other than sealing and mixing waste items (metabolic and non-metabolic), followed by manual compaction and temporary storage intocargo vehicles and subsequent disposal (return to earth or destructive re-entry). This approach to waste management is unfeasible to sustain, especially in missions with increased distance from Earth (e.g. lunar outpost surface missions) and reduced frequency of re-supply. MELiSSA C1 Waste Compartment is the only waste biodegradation process envisaged so far for space applications in Europe. Yet, its complete microbial consortium and dynamics remain unknown and it is fully devoted to transform the metabolic waste derived from the crewed mission.This activity aims at improving the waste management strategy for future missions beyond LEO byexpanding the waste input suitable for the MELiSSA Waste Compartment. This approach supports the creation of a synthetic microbial community capable of transforming both metabolic and nonmetabolic waste. This is atechnology push to explore improved robustness and efficiency of the C1 consortium specifically in view of the capability to adapt towaste from packaging.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of existing microbial communities ubiquitously present in the MELiSSA anaerobic bioreactor which are capable of biodegrading the alternative packaging material developed in a previous activity. Compatibility with key microbial consortium and operating conditionsin MELiSSA anaerobic bioreactor shall be addressed.-Microbial consortium complementation and preliminary full testing of the metabolic and nonmetabolicwaste degradation efficiency. Special attention shall be paid to the population dynamics and resilience, macro- and micro-compounds mass balances, energy balances,methanogenesis inhibition and inhibition of secondary toxic metabolites formation during the conversion process.- The update of mathematical models equations to transform the mechanistic model of the waste anaerobic bioreactor into a white-box model.
